run.question: In the elasticsearch index 'app-276-logs-9j2k4p7m', run a `terms: { level: ["ERROR", "FATAL"] }` query and tell me how many hits come back. If that returns zero, find the right field for log severity and re-run the query.

report.summary: The requested query does return zero hits: a `terms` query on field `level` with values ["ERROR","FATAL"] against app-276-logs-9j2k4p7m returned total 0 (relation eq), and a terms aggregation on `level` returned no buckets. The reason is visible in the index mapping: the index has no `level` field at all; its properties are `@timestamp` (date), `msg` (text), `severity_num` (integer) and `svc` (keyword). Re-running the severity filter on the field that actually exists, `severity_num`, restricted to 5 and 6, returned 8 hits: 6 documents with severity_num=5 and 2 with severity_num=6, all with svc=order-276. The severity-to-number mapping is visible in the documents themselves: severity_num=5 carries msgs '[ERROR] DB timeout 1'..'6', severity_num=6 carries '[FATAL] Disk full 1'..'2', severity_num=4 carries '[WARN] Slow query 1'..'5' and severity_num=3 carries '[INFO] Order placed 1'..'10'. An independent cross-check with a query_string on `msg` for ERROR or FATAL also returned 8, so the two paths agree. All 23 documents in the index fell inside the one-hour window the search tool applied (2026-11-22T09:31:24Z to 10:31:24Z): the ERROR burst ran 10:27:01–10:27:06Z and the FATAL pair 10:28:01–10:28:02Z. No root cause object is named: this Run only exercised the log index, and no evidence ties the failures to a specific Kubernetes object or configuration.

claims.text: Index app-276-logs-9j2k4p7m is open and green with docs.count 23 and store.size 9.2kb at the moment of the query.
The mapping of app-276-logs-9j2k4p7m contains only four properties: @timestamp (date), msg (text), severity_num (integer) and svc (keyword). There is no `level` field.

The requested query {"terms":{"level":["ERROR","FATAL"]}} on app-276-logs-9j2k4p7m returned total value 0 (relation eq) under the tool's @timestamp filter 2026-11-22T09:31:24Z to 2026-11-22T10:31:24Z; the accompanying terms aggregation on `level` returned zero buckets.

The severity field that exists, severity_num, distributes across the 23 documents in the window as: key 3 with 10 docs, key 4 with 5 docs, key 5 with 6 docs, key 6 with 2 docs; all 23 documents have svc=order-276.

The documents show the severity_num convention: severity_num=5 pairs with msgs '[ERROR] DB timeout 1' through '[ERROR] DB timeout 6', severity_num=6 with '[FATAL] Disk full 1' and '[FATAL] Disk full 2', severity_num=4 with '[WARN] Slow query 1'-'5', and severity_num=3 with '[INFO] Order placed 1'-'10'.

Re-running the severity filter on the correct field, {"terms":{"severity_num":[5,6]}}, returned total value 8 in the same window: 6 documents with severity_num=5 ([ERROR] DB timeout 1-6, 10:27:01Z-10:27:06Z) and 2 with severity_num=6 ([FATAL] Disk full 1-2, 10:28:01Z-10:28:02Z), all svc=order-276.
An independent cross-check using a query_string msg:(ERROR or FATAL) on the text field returned total value 8, agreeing with the severity_num=5,6 count.
The '[ERROR] DB timeout' messages suggest a database or dependency timeout behind the order-276 logging workload, but this Run queried only the log index, so the timing-out dependency is unconfirmed.
Query severity with severity_num (5=ERROR, 6=FATAL) or with a msg text match on this index; do not use a `level` field, which is not mapped here.

gaps: The searches were executed with the tool's default 1-hour @timestamp filter (2026-11-22T09:31:24Z to 10:31:24Z), not the full 24-hour authorized window 2026-11-21T10:31:24Z to 2026-11-22T10:31:24Z; log content older than that hour was not examined and is unknown.

No documents, traces, metrics or Kubernetes objects were examined to attribute the [ERROR] DB timeout or [FATAL] Disk full messages to a specific service, pod, workload or configuration object, so the underlying cause and the affected entity beyond svc=order-276 in these log documents remain unknown.
The mapping does not document what values severity_num may take beyond the 3,4,5,6 observed; whether other severity levels exist was not verifiable.
next_steps: Inspect the logs for svc=order-276 as a workload (Kubernetes pod/deployment status, container restarts, events) and correlate the 10:27:01Z-10:28:02Z window with traces and metrics to identify the timing-out database dependency.
If this index is written by a log pipeline, consider adding a normalized severity keyword field so `level`-style queries work without knowing the numeric encoding.
